judged_text: The uniqueGuests filter only removes emails matching existing attendees and never deduplicates the input array itself, while the server schema (addGuests.schema.ts line 5) omits the uniqueness .refine that the client-side copy in AddGuestsDialog enforces. A direct addGuests mutation with ['a@b.com','a@b.com'] passes both gates and createMany inserts two Attendee rows with the same email, so the guest receives two identical scheduled-confirmation emails and appears twice on the calendar event — the uniqueness invariant exists only in the client schema, which any API caller bypasses.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: server input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (packages/trpc/.../addGuests.schema.ts) only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce uniqueness, while the client dialog uses a local Zod schema with `.refine` for uniqueness (apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx). In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees/blacklisted emails but does not dedupe duplicates within the `guests` array itself; thus `['a@b.com','a@b.com']` can produce two entries in `guestsFullDetails` and be inserted via `attendees.createMany`. The subsequent attendee list is built from `bookingAttendees.attendees`, so duplicates would also propagate into email sending/calendar updates.
